title: Let AI Write Your Excel Formulas (Works in Google Sheets Too)
short_title: Get any Excel formula in seconds with AI
description:
Stop searching for Excel formulas. In this video you'll learn how to describe what you want in plain English and let a free AI chatbot write the formula for you: SUMIFS totals, XLOOKUP lookups, late-invoice flags and cleaning messy data. Plus how to get any formula explained and fix errors fast. Works in Excel and Google Sheets.

Subscribe to Work Hacked for a new work shortcut every week.

This video uses AI-generated narration and visuals.

#excel #AItools #productivity

scenes.narration: Excel formulas can take forever to figure out. Today I'll show you how to get any formula you need in seconds, just by describing it in plain English.
This works with ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini or any free AI chatbot, and the formulas work in both Excel and Google Sheets.
Here's the secret. Don't just say, give me a formula. Tell the AI three things.
Example one. You have sales in a table. Region is in column B, and the amount is in column C. You want the total for the East region only.

screen.user: Region is in column B, sales amount in column C. Give me a formula for the total sales for the East region.

scenes.narration: Paste it in, and the answer appears instantly. No more adding numbers by hand or filtering the table.
Example two. You have a product list, and you need to find a price by its product code. This is called a lookup, and it confuses a lot of people.

screen.user: Product codes are in column A, prices in column D. Find the price for the code typed in F2. Show Not found if it's missing.

scenes.narration: Type a code, and the price shows up. If the code doesn't exist, you see Not found instead of an ugly error.
Example three. You want to flag invoices that are more than thirty days old, so you know who to chase for payment.

screen.user: Invoice dates are in column D. Show Late if the date is more than 30 days ago, otherwise OK.

scenes.narration: Put it in the first row, drag it down, and every invoice is checked automatically, every single day.
Example four, cleaning messy data. Names with extra spaces, or all in capital letters? One short formula fixes them.
Now a pro tip. If you don't understand a formula, someone else's or one the AI gave you, paste it in and ask the AI to explain it step by step.

screen.user: Explain this formula step by step in simple words: =SUMIFS(C:C, B:B, "East")
screen.ai: It adds up the numbers in column C, but only on rows where column B says East.

scenes.narration: And if a formula gives you an error, copy the error message and paste it back to the AI. It will usually tell you exactly what went wrong.

screen.user: My formula shows #N/A. What does that mean and how do I fix it?
screen.ai: #N/A means the value wasn't found. Check for extra spaces or a different spelling.

scenes.narration: One warning. Always test a new formula on a copy of your file, and check a few results by hand before you trust it.

screen.title: Before you trust a formula
items: Check a few results by hand
Make sure the ranges are right

scenes.narration: So, describe your columns, say what you want, and let AI write the formula. Then test it.
Try it on your own spreadsheet today, and subscribe to Work Hacked for a new work shortcut every week.
